system.summary: Homophonic letter table plus a one-part nomenclator. 24 letters with three two-digit homophones each, 24 apart (A = 16, 40, 64); consecutive letters 4 apart in runs of six (A-F 16-36, G-M 17-37, N-S 18-38, T-Z 19-39). 23 serves for U and V; W (27), Y (35), Z (39) unused in these letters. Three-digit codes 187-760 in alphabetical order of their meanings, with Latin endings written in clear beside them. Only key words are enciphered; the rest of the Latin is clear.
system.sibling_key: None used. R4333-R4335 (the other Rusdorff letters in E 701) use another system: R4333 is German with numbers 8-13 and 100-107, outside this table; DECODE lists R4334 and R4335 as 'Alphabet'.
system.notes: 38 distinct code values in lasry2026/ctts/key.txt (one, 747, a tentative second code for the King of Sweden besides 746). Homophones: three per letter by construction (n, n+24, n+48); not all occur in these letters.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment found (21 Oct 2026): DECODE R4336/R4337 Non-decrypted with images only; nothing on Cryptoole (XX1628-11), Cryptiana or in Waldispühl & Kopal. Kröger, Johann von Rusdorf (1876) pp. 9-10 reports Rusdorf's own copybook of his correspondence with Oxenstierna 1624-1628 as vol. 3 of his papers at the Landesbibliothek Kassel (now UB Kassel), unprinted in 1876. It probably holds the clear text of these letters; not consulted, not found digitised.

conditions.human_role: George Lasry transcribed the five images in CTTS, ran CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis for the letter table, directed Claude Opus 5.5 on the three-digit codes, edited the Latin, translated it and wrote the historical context; contributed as PR 72. In this repository: merge, split from rusdorff1628, prior-solution search, mechanical check and statistical validation.
tools: CTTS (CrypTool Transcriber and Solver): transcription and built-in cryptanalysis

solution.what: Project survey of catalogue 207: fetched DECODE R4333-R4337 with the project cookie; Rusdorff's letters to Oxenstierna, catalogued The Hague 1628, figures inside clear text. Not transcribed.
George Lasry transcribed R4336 (2 images) and R4337 (3 images) in CTTS, boxing each two-digit group, three-digit code and clear segment: 438 cipher tokens (376 letter signs, 62 codes).

CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis gave the initial homophonic letter table; George Lasry completed it with the 24-step rule (homophones n, n+24, n+48; letters 4 apart in runs of six), which every letter occurrence then fits.

Claude Opus 5.5, directed by George Lasry, recovered the three-digit codes from context and the Latin endings written beside them (-is, -to, -bus, -m), checked against the alphabetical order of the nomenclator (187 Britannicus ... 760 Rusdorff): 36 occurrences confident, 24 tentative, 2 unknown (628, 701).

George Lasry edited the Latin of the three letters (London 15/25 Feb 1625; London 26 Feb 1625 old style, signed Rusdorff; an undated further letter), translated it and dated the letters from their text: London 1625, not The Hague 1628 as catalogued (PR 72).

Prior-solution check: DECODE R4336/R4337 Non-decrypted, no documents attached; nothing on Cryptoole, Cryptiana or in Waldispühl & Kopal; no printed decipherment found. Kröger 1876 reports Rusdorf's copybook of his Oxenstierna letters 1624-1628 at Kassel, unprinted in 1876: a probable clear-text source, not consulted. Riksarkivet's Oxenstierna letter database is behind a CAPTCHA and was not searched.

Merged PR 72 and split R4336/R4337 from rusdorff1628 under the one-key rule: R4333 (German, numbers 8-13 and 100-107) cannot be in this table, and DECODE lists R4334/R4335 as 'Alphabet'. decode.py re-applies key.txt to the CTTS transcription and reproduces George's counts exactly: 376 letter signs, all assigned; 62 codes, 36 confident, 24 tentative, 2 unknown.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 376 tokens, 48 types, la order 4: reading -1.997 per letter; random keys -5.2 (z 7.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.684 (mean -2.724, z 28.5); annealer on the real text -2.545. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.997; polyphony 0.0; 62 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.545

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry recovered the letter table with CTTS's cryptanalysis and the 24-step rule, and the codes with Claude Opus 5.5 from context and the nomenclator's alphabetical order; no clear copy or outside key was used.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py --counts: 436 of 438 cipher tokens carry a value (376 letter signs, 60 codes); 2 codes unknown (628, 701). 24 of the 60 code readings are tentative.

credits.note: Transcribed with CTTS; letter table from CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis; three-digit codes recovered with Claude Opus 5.5; edited Latin, translation and context.

gaps.detail: Alphabetical ranges Palatinatus-Papista and Propositio-Regnum; no second occurrence. Rusdorf's Kassel copybook (Kröger 1876) would settle them and the 24 tentative codes; not consulted.

gaps.item: First page of the 26 February letter, the subscription of the 15/25 February letter and the rest of the third letter
gaps.detail: Not among the DECODE photographs of E 701.

texts.label: R4336, London, 15/25 Feb 1625
texts.summary: Rusdorff has seen the secret Swedish proposals put to Anstruther for restoring the Palatinate; London leans to Christian IV, whose terms are modest (6,000 foot and 1,000 horse asked, 4,000 and 1,000 offered).

texts.label: R4337, London, 26 Feb 1625 (o.s.) and a further undated letter
texts.summary: Buckingham prepares to fetch the French bride but the papal dispensation and Parliament stand in the way; France offers 500,000 livres to the confederation on condition of joint arbitration in Germany.
